title: Policy for Trading in Company Securities

tiers.name: Paladin Personnel
tiers.description: Executive and non-executive directors; officers, the Company Secretary, senior managers and executives; full-time, part-time and casual employees; and contractors, suppliers, consultants, agents, representatives and advisers of Paladin, Paladin group companies and joint ventures under Paladin's operational control. Bound by the insider trading prohibition and by the ban on hedging incentive securities, but not by the permission to Trade regime or the blackout periods unless also a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: A Director or employee who, due to seniority or role, is likely to come into possession of Material Information: Paladin's directors, CEO, CFO, Company Secretary, General Managers, any other person in a managerial position reporting directly to the CEO or CFO, and executive assistants to those persons. The Company Secretary maintains a register of Restricted Persons and monitors their Trading. Subject to blackout periods, the permission to Trade regime, the financing and hedging approval requirement, and the short selling and 90-day bans.

tiers.name: Closely Connected Persons
tiers.description: A spouse or de facto partner of a Restricted Person, a child or dependant of a Restricted Person, and a company or trust controlled by, or in which a beneficial interest is held by, such a spouse, partner, child or dependant. Subject to the same blackout periods and restrictions; the Restricted Person must take all reasonable steps to ensure they do not Trade without permission and applies on their behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: you must not enter into margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin’s securities, and you must not deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements in relation to Paladin’s securities, that would have the effect of limiting your exposure to risk in relation to part or all of your remuneration that has not vested, or has vested but remains subject to a restriction arrangement (e.g. a holding lock). For the purposes of this Policy, this prohibition applies to any contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Paladin’s securities

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may vary the blackout periods, circulated with appropriate notice to all Restricted Persons; the variation is therefore notified rather than confidential. Separately, permission to Trade will generally not be granted where Paladin is considering a market announcement or is relying on the continuous disclosure exception, where the Authorising Officer considers there is undisclosed price sensitive information, or where there is a risk the market will suspect the applicant had Inside Information or a risk of reputational damage; a refusal must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: Over vested unrestricted securities that were not granted under an employee incentive scheme, an OTC put and call is possible but doubly gated: the Board's approval is required for the hedging arrangement, and because 'securities' expressly includes over-the-counter options and 'Trade' includes creating a hedge, the Authorising Officer's permission to Trade is also required and the transaction must fall outside a blackout period.
rules.evidence: you must obtain the Board’s approval to enter into a margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin’s securities, providing the Board with the material terms of the proposed arrangements, including the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and trigger events;

rules.detail: Absolute ban on dealing in derivatives or entering other arrangements in relation to Paladin's securities that limit exposure to risk on unvested remuneration. No approval route; the Board's approval power applies to the financing and hedging arrangements permitted by the first bullet, not to this prohibition.
rules.evidence: you must not deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements in relation to Paladin’s securities, that would have the effect of limiting your exposure to risk in relation to part or all of your remuneration that has not vested

rules.detail: The same absolute ban extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a restriction arrangement such as a holding lock, so shares still inside a holding lock cannot be collared even with Board approval.
rules.evidence: or has vested but remains subject to a restriction arrangement (e.g. a holding lock)

rules.detail: Personnel who are not Restricted Persons are not subject to the permission to Trade regime, the blackout periods or the section 6 financing and derivatives restrictions, which are prefaced 'if you are a Restricted Person or a Closely Connected Person'. Only the insider trading prohibition and the ban on hedging incentive securities apply to them.
rules.evidence: Further, if you are a Restricted Person or a Closely Connected Person:

rules.detail: Blanket ban, applying to everyone within the Policy and not just Restricted Persons, on hedging securities granted as incentives under any Paladin employee incentive scheme. Put/call arrangements are named as a prohibited hedging practice.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from hedging securities granted as incentives under any Paladin employee incentive scheme. This relates to both vested and unvested securities. Prohibited hedging practices include put/call arrangements over “in-the-money” rights to hedge against a future drop in share price.

rules.detail: Critically for a collar, the incentive-securities hedging ban is expressed to survive vesting: it 'relates to both vested and unvested securities'. Shares in hand that originated from an LTI or STI grant can never be collared, no matter how long ago they vested or who approves. Only securities acquired otherwise (for example bought on market) fall outside this ban.
rules.evidence: You are prohibited from hedging securities granted as incentives under any Paladin employee incentive scheme. This relates to both vested and unvested securities.

rules.detail: A hedging arrangement in relation to Paladin's securities that were not granted as incentives, and that does not limit exposure to unvested or locked remuneration, is permitted with the Board's approval, which must be sought on the material terms including the lender's unilateral sale rights and trigger events.
rules.evidence: you must obtain the Board’s approval to enter into a margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin’s securities

rules.detail: Hedging that limits exposure to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock or other restriction arrangement is prohibited outright, with no Board approval route.
rules.evidence: you must not enter into margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin’s securities ... that would have the effect of limiting your exposure to risk in relation to part or all of your remuneration that ... has vested but remains subject to a restriction arrangement (e.g. a holding lock).

rules.detail: Prepaid forwards, collar loans and similar monetisations are not named. They are Trades (creating a hedge, security interest or other financial interest over securities, or agreeing to do so) and are also 'secured financing arrangements in relation to Paladin's securities', so they need both Board approval and permission to Trade. Where the monetised parcel is incentive-granted, unvested or holding-locked, they are prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to securities;

rules.detail: Flat ban for Restricted Persons and Closely Connected Persons; no equivalent express ban on other Paladin Personnel.
rules.evidence: you must not engage in short selling Paladin’s securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named, but transferring legal ownership of securities even where beneficial ownership does not change, and creating any other financial interest in securities, are Trades, so a stock loan requires permission to Trade and cannot be done in a blackout period. Lending to facilitate a short position would also engage the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: transferring legal ownership of securities, even where beneficial ownership does not change;

rules.detail: CFDs are named. The sentence sits within the bullet dealing with unvested and holding-locked remuneration but is expressed to apply to 'any contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Paladin's securities', which reads as a free-standing ban.
rules.evidence: For the purposes of this Policy, this prohibition applies to any contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Paladin’s securities;

rules.detail: Margin lending in relation to Paladin's securities is permitted with prior Board approval, on disclosure of the material terms including the lender's right to sell unilaterally and trigger events, and with an ongoing duty to keep the Company Secretary informed of changes relevant to continuous disclosure.
rules.evidence: you must obtain the Board’s approval to enter into a margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin’s securities, providing the Board with the material terms of the proposed arrangements, including the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and trigger events;

rules.detail: Margin lending that has the effect of limiting exposure to risk on unvested remuneration, or on remuneration vested but subject to a restriction arrangement, is prohibited with no approval route.
rules.evidence: you must not enter into margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin’s securities ... that would have the effect of limiting your exposure to risk in relation to part or all of your remuneration that has not vested

rules.detail: Creating a security interest over Paladin securities is itself a Trade, so it requires permission to Trade from the Authorising Officer and cannot occur in a blackout period; if it secures a financing it also requires Board approval. Pledging unvested or holding-locked remuneration in a way that limits risk exposure is prohibited.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to securities;

rules.detail: The catch-all 'any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin's securities' is permitted with Board approval, which makes this policy one of the few that contemplates a bank facility secured on the shares. The Board must be given the material terms, specifically including the lender's unilateral sale right and the trigger events.
rules.evidence: you must obtain the Board’s approval to enter into a margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin’s securities, providing the Board with the material terms of the proposed arrangements, including the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and trigger events;

rules.detail: Secured financing over remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock or other restriction arrangement, where it limits risk exposure, is prohibited and the Board cannot approve it.
rules.evidence: you must not enter into margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin’s securities ... in relation to part or all of your remuneration that ... has vested but remains subject to a restriction arrangement (e.g. a holding lock).

rules.detail: Restricted Persons and Closely Connected Persons must not engage in short term (less than 90 days) or speculative trading in Paladin's securities or in financial products associated with Paladin's securities; Trading for short term or speculative gain is also prohibited at all times under the blackout clause. No carve-outs are stated.
rules.evidence: you must not engage in ‘short term’ (less than 90 days) or speculative trading in Paladin’s securities or in financial products associated with Paladin’s securities;

clearance.approver: Authorising Officer: Paladin's Chairperson for directors (excluding the Chairperson), the CEO or the Company Secretary and their Closely Connected Persons; Paladin's Company Secretary for any other person (including the Chairperson) and their Closely Connected Persons. The Authorising Officer must first consult the Disclosure Committee. Board approval is separately required for margin lending, hedging and other secured financing arrangements.
clearance.post_trade_to: the Authorising Officer who gave permission (confirmation that the Trade has occurred and details of the price per security)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: following completion of the Trade; no fixed deadline stated
clearance.evidence: If permission to Trade is given, such permission: is valid for five business days, unless the written permission to Trade specifies another period; can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances; and is not an endorsement of the proposed Trade.

clearance.approver: The same Authorising Officer, on an application made by the Restricted Person on the Closely Connected Person's behalf
clearance.post_trade_to: the Authorising Officer who gave permission
clearance.post_trade_deadline: following completion of the Trade; no fixed deadline stated
clearance.evidence: A Restricted Person must not, and must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Closely Connected Persons do not, Trade in securities without the Restricted Person obtaining permission to do so under this Policy.
Additional restrictions are placed on Trading by Restricted Persons. Annexure A of this Policy sets out who is considered to be a Restricted Person.

short_term.basis: less than 90 days; extends to financial products associated with Paladin's securities
short_term.evidence: you must not engage in ‘short term’ (less than 90 days) or speculative trading in Paladin’s securities or in financial products associated with Paladin’s securities;

exceptions.evidence: (takeover or scheme) results from a scheme of arrangement or acceptance of a takeover offer;

(pro rata offers) relates to dealings under an offer or invitation made to all or most shareholders or class of shareholders, such as a disposal of Paladin securities arising from the acceptance of an equal access buy-back or an acquisition of Paladin securities under a pro rata issue;

(security purchase plans and dividend reinvestment plans) arises under an offer to some or all holders of Paladin’s securities under a security purchase plan or dividend reinvestment plan, provided that you comply with the provisions of the plan and do not commence, terminate or amend your participation in the plan during a “blackout” period

(incentive scheme) results from the exercise (but not a Trade following exercise) of an option or performance right under a Paladin employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security ... where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or conversion of the security, falls during a “blackout” period and you could not reasonably be expected to have exercised the option or right during a permitted trading period.

exceptions.approver: Authorising Officer (Chairperson or Company Secretary), after consulting the Disclosure Committee
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship – an immediate and pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant securities;
where there is a court order or other legal or regulatory obligation to transfer or accept a transfer of Paladin’s securities;
other circumstances determined by the Authorising Officer to be exceptional.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No loan-to-value ratio, buffer or price trigger level is prescribed, but the Board must be given the material terms of the proposed arrangement, expressly including the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and the trigger events, before approving it.
financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons and Closely Connected Persons: at inception, before entering into any margin lending, hedging or other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin's securities, provide the Board with the material terms including the lender's right to sell unilaterally and trigger events, as part of obtaining the Board's approval.

Restricted Persons and Closely Connected Persons with an approved arrangement: on any change in circumstances that may be relevant to Paladin's continuous disclosure obligations, keep the Company Secretary informed; no deadline stated.
Directors and executive officers: maintain current insider filings of their Trades with the applicable securities regulatory authorities (TSX / Ontario).
All Paladin Personnel: on request, provide details about any Trading in Paladin's securities and respond in a timely manner.

external_documents: Continuous Disclosure & Communications Policy (establishes the Disclosure Committee the Authorising Officer must consult)

exemption_authority: The Board may approve margin lending, hedging and other secured financing arrangements in relation to Paladin's securities, and may vary the blackout periods. An Authorising Officer (the Chairperson or the Company Secretary) may permit a Trade, including a sale during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances, after consulting the Disclosure Committee, and may give or refuse permission without reasons. No one may authorise hedging of securities granted under an employee incentive scheme, or any arrangement limiting exposure to unvested or holding-locked remuneration.
jurisdiction_overlays: Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and ASX Listing Rules
Securities Act (Ontario) and TSX listing rules, including insider reporting/filing obligations for directors and executive officers

bespoke_clauses.clause: you must obtain the Board's approval to enter into a margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin's securities, providing the Board with the material terms of the proposed arrangements, including the right of the lender to sell unilaterally and trigger events
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an affirmative approval pathway for both the hedge and the secured loan of a funded collar, but the bank must expect its unilateral sale rights, LVR triggers and termination events to be disclosed to and scrutinised by the full Board before signing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: incentive securities hedging ban survives vesting
bespoke_clauses.clause: You are prohibited from hedging securities granted as incentives under any Paladin employee incentive scheme. This relates to both vested and unvested securities. Prohibited hedging practices include put/call arrangements over 'in-the-money' rights to hedge against a future drop in share price.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares that originated from an LTI or STI grant can never be collared even long after vesting, so the collateral pool must be limited to securities acquired outside the incentive schemes and the bank needs provenance evidence for every share pledged.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Prohibited hedging practices include put/call arrangements over 'in-the-money' rights to hedge against a future drop in share price.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The exact structure of a collar is named as a prohibited practice for incentive securities, so there is no scope to argue the ban was not aimed at this product.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you must not enter into margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement ... that would have the effect of limiting your exposure to risk in relation to part or all of your remuneration that has not vested, or has vested but remains subject to a restriction arrangement (e.g. a holding lock).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Board approval cannot cure a hedge over unvested or holding-locked remuneration, so the collateral must be free of any restriction arrangement at the time the collar is struck.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the purposes of this Policy, this prohibition applies to any contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of Paladin's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cash-settled collar is a contract intended to avoid a loss based on price fluctuations, so any cash-settled variant risks being caught by this catch-all even where the underlying shares are freely held.

bespoke_clauses.topic: creating a hedge or security interest is a Trade
bespoke_clauses.clause: Trade or Trading includes: ... creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to securities; transferring legal ownership of securities, even where beneficial ownership does not change; ... and agreeing or applying to do any of the above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Signing the collar, granting the security and transferring the shares to a custodian or the bank's nominee are each separate Trades needing permission and falling outside blackout periods, and even the agreement to do so is caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: securities Includes ... any derivatives of those securities (including equity swaps, contracts for difference, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue or settlement-method gap: an OTC, cash-settled bank option is a Paladin security for every purpose of the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If permission to Trade is given, such permission is valid for five business days, unless the written permission to Trade specifies another period; can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution must complete within five business days unless a longer bespoke period is negotiated in the written permission, and the permission remains withdrawable until the transaction is done.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any permission to Trade can be given or refused, without giving any reasons. ... The decision to refuse permission is final and binding ... If permission to Trade is refused, the Restricted Person seeking the permission must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive cannot tell the bank why a collar entry, roll or unwind is blocked, so the documentation needs an unexplained termination or extension right.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Permission to Trade will generally not be granted if ... there is a risk the market will suspect the person seeking permission to trade had Inside Information, or there is a risk of reputational damage to Paladin.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a fully compliant collar can be refused on optics alone, which makes any committed bank facility contingent on a discretionary judgement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the periods commencing from the end of: a financial quarter up to the day after the release date of the quarter's results; a half-year ...; and a financial year ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a quarterly reporter Paladin closes the window four times a year, so execution and any unwind must be timed to the narrow post-release periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if you have entered into any margin lending arrangement, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement with the Board's approval, you must keep the Company Secretary informed of any change in circumstances that may be relevant to Paladin's continuous disclosure obligations
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Amendments, LVR breaches or enforcement steps under the facility must be reported to the Company Secretary on an ongoing basis and may become publicly disclosed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not, and must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Closely Connected Persons do not, Trade in securities without the Restricted Person obtaining permission to do so under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a spouse's name or a family trust does not avoid the approval, blackout or hedging restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no closed-period relief for anything but a sale
bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances, permission may be given by an Authorising Officer for a Restricted Person or their Closely Connected Person to Trade securities in Paladin (where such Trade only involves a proposed sale of securities) during a 'blackout' period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Blackout relief is available only for outright sales, so a collar cannot be struck, rolled or hedged during a blackout even in hardship.

summary: A funded collar is possible for a Paladin Restricted Person, but only over a narrow slice of stock and only with Board sign-off. Section 6 expressly contemplates 'margin lending, hedging or any other secured financing arrangement in relation to Paladin's securities' with the Board's approval, given on disclosure of the material terms including the lender's right to sell unilaterally and the trigger events, which covers both the option legs and the loan secured on the collared shares. The decisive limitation is the collateral pool: hedging of securities granted under any Paladin employee incentive scheme is prohibited outright and expressly 'relates to both vested and unvested securities', and no arrangement may limit exposure to remuneration that is unvested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock, so only shares acquired outside the incentive schemes can be collared and provenance must be evidenced. Execution also needs the Authorising Officer's written permission to Trade (Chairperson for directors, CEO and Company Secretary; Company Secretary for everyone else), which lasts five business days, may be withdrawn, may be refused without reasons or on reputational grounds alone, and cannot be given during the quarterly, half-year and full-year blackout periods except for an outright sale. Tenor must exceed 90 days to avoid the short-term trading ban, cash-settled structures risk the contracts-for-difference catch-all, and any later change to the facility must be reported to the Company Secretary for continuous disclosure purposes.
